subject: Service-level addendum: proposed latency tiers & procurement runbook
messages:
From: Anna Blake <anna.blake@optimahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Optima Health Procurement <procurement@optimahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tailored SLA addendum + evidence mapping for order form

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to consolidate Optima's non-standard SLA asks so we can put language into our MSA / Order Form. High level: we need explicit latency tiers for inference (p95), corresponding uptime commitments, and the evidence the vendor will provide when those commitments are invoked.

Key items from our side:
- Tier A (critical): p95 <= 150ms, 99.95% uptime for production endpoints (customer-facing features)
- Tier B (standard): p95 <= 400ms, 99.9% uptime for background/async endpoints
- Clear playbook for incidents that might trigger credits: what telemetry you’ll share, minimum retention windows, and the runbook we can rely on for audit
- KMS compatibility + HIPAA-friendly controls — our security team will follow up with specifics

Can Redwood draft an SLA addendum + a short procurement runbook that maps each latency/tier to the expected evidence payload (e.g., per-request traces, per-route latency histograms, token counts, KV-cache logs) and DOC/SLA language we can attach to the Order Form? Ideally we can get a redline back this week so our legal and procurement can start integrating.

I’m looping in Procurement on this thread. Let me know if we should do a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Anna Blake
Sr. Procurement Manager | Optima Health
attachments: optima_requested_tiers.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Blake <anna.blake@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Optima Health Procurement <procurement@optimahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Sep 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA addendum + evidence mapping for order form

Thanks Anna — great level-setting.

We can absolutely produce a targeted SLA addendum that includes:
- A two-tier latency+uptime matrix mapped to order form exhibit language
- A concise evidence runbook itemizing telemetry artifacts we will provide per incident (and standard retention windows)
- An appendix describing fallback model variants and regional routing for resilience

Action plan I propose:
1) I’ll attach an initial redline draft of the SLA addendum and a draft runbook mapping (see attached: optima_sla_redlines_v1.pdf + procurement_runbook_draft.xlsx)
2) Kimberly will own the order-form exhibit language and the Docusign execution path
3) If Optima’s CISO wants to confirm KMS/HSM details, we’ll bring in Rishi to map the security evidence set

Can we do a 30-min sync on Wednesday 9/4 or Thursday 9/5? I’ve tentatively blocked time in the HubSpot invite (link below).

Next steps: please review the redline and call out any absolute no-go clauses so we don’t chase incompatible edits.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: review of Optima SLA redline + evidence runbook

Aditya / Rishi — quick internal notes before we send to Optima:

On the redline:
- The draft uses "per-route p95 latency" as the observable. That’s OK but we should define sampling rules (1:1000) and a fallback path to full sampling for forensics (cost + retention caveats).
- Proposed retention: 90 days for aggregated histograms; 365 days for incident-specific raw traces on request (with cost recovery).
- Credits language: tie credits to monthly measured uptime per order form; add a 30-day dispute window.

Security/evidence mapping (Rishi to weigh in):
- Rishi: we should map Tier A to a full evidence bundle: request-level trace (anonymized), kv-cache hit rates, host-level GPU telemetry, and storage of audit logs in a customer-accessible s3 bucket (read-only).
- For on-prem or VPC installs we’ll indicate KMS/HSM support and propose a security questionnaire appendix (SOC 2 + configuration checklist).

Procurement flow:
- Kimberly will update order form exhibit language to include a checkbox for "Tier A" vs "Tier B" pricing and a link to the runbook.
- Marissa — FYI on discount / uplift discussion: if customer selects Tier A for > 3 production routes, we treat as dedicated pool discussion (pricing follow-up).

I’ll propose concrete text in the order form exhibit by EOD Thursday so Aditya has something to send to Anna prior to the sync.

-Kimberly
Director, Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference
attachments: latency_tier_mapping.png (diagram stub)

Date: Thu, 5 Sep 2029 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: tailored SLA addendum + evidence mapping for order form

Hi Aditya / Kimberly,

Thanks for the draft — a few security/ops clarifications before we proceed to legal redlines:

1) KMS/HSM: we need confirmation that Redwood supports customer-managed keys in the VPC/private deployment path. If yes, what KMS vendors and HSM models have you validated?
2) Evidence artifacts: raw traces must be pseudonymized; please confirm the default anonymization approach and whether we can request raw ids for specific investigations (with an audit log).
3) Telemetry retention & access: for Tier A we require telemetry retention of 180 days for per-request traces (with a clearly priced retrieval SLA).
4) Billing trigger: if credits are requested, please outline the exact measurement window and whether credits apply as percentage of monthly invoice or as service credits only.

Also — can you provide a short timeline for a PoC that validates p95 at the Tier A threshold under our payload (we have a small test harness we can share)? Procurement wants to see execution milestones tied to order form acceptance.

Thanks,
Daniel Hsu
CISO | Optima Health
attachments: security_questions_optima.docx (stub)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Hsu <d.hsu@optimahealth.com>, Anna Blake <anna.blake@optimahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Sep 2029 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA addendum + evidence mapping for order form

Daniel / Anna — thanks for the clear asks. Summarizing Redwood’s commit and the next steps so procurement/legal have a single reference:

Proposed language and commitments (high level):
- Latency tiers: Tier A (p95 <= 150ms) / Tier B (p95 <= 400ms); order form will include a selectable Exhibit A with the chosen routes listed and the effective start date.
- Uptime: Tier A: 99.95% monthly; Tier B: 99.9% monthly. Credits computed as percentage-of-monthly-service (exhibit to define exact credit bands).
- Evidence bundle for Tier A incidents: pseudonymized request traces, per-route p95 histograms, KV-cache hit rates, relevant host GPU telemetry, and a signed incident summary. Default retention: 180 days for incident-level traces; 90 days aggregated metrics. Retrieval SLA: 10 business days (expedited at cost).
- KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys for VPC/private deployments (AWS KMS and AWS CloudHSM validated; GCP KMS available via partner config). We’ll include a configuration appendix for the Order Form.
- PoC: proposed 4-week PoC window after order form acceptance (week 0: instrumentation + test harness; weeks 1–3: load and p95 validation).

Procurement/Execution path:
- Kimberly will attach the updated Exhibit A (order form) and route to DocuSign after Optima marks the Tier selection.
- Rishi will produce the security appendix and the SOC2 configuration checklist.
- Marissa will coordinate pricing uplift guidance if Tier A selected across > 3 production routes.

Attached to this message are the redline and the draft runbook mapping. Please review and call out any critical objections in reply. If none, Kimberly will route the DocuSign path by Friday 9/13.

Thanks all — happy to jump on a quick call if it helps finalize language.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
